api/Global.LHH_TestSDK.html.summary: Class LHH_TestSDK Entry point for automated tests against a device build from the Unity Editor (NUnit, Edit Mode or Play Mode). Inheritance Object LHH_TestSDK Namespace: Global Assembly: LHH.TestSDK.Docs.dll Syntax public sealed class LHH_TestSDK : MonoBehaviour Remarks First API call on a run: connect to Test Controller, lease device, Appium session, wait for player hub. Configure via menu LHH Test SDK - Settings (gRPC, platform, app path, bundle id). Requires LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST and a running Test Controller. Editor-only; not in player builds. Methods CleanUpAfterTest() Returns the leased device to the Test Controller and resets setup state for the next run. Declaration public static void CleanUpAfterTest() Remarks The Test Runner invokes this when a run finishes or errors only if LHH_TestSDKSettings.ReleaseSessionAfterTestRun is enabled (default on). Use Release session now in Settings or call this manually for early teardown. ClickButton(string, float) Waits for a UI object, then invokes its Unity UI Button onClick in the running game. Declaration public static Task ClickButton(string buttonPath, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string buttonPath Hierarchy path with / separators (root via GameObject.Find, children via Transform.Find). float timeoutSeconds Maximum seconds to wait for the button object before failing. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use, then WaitForObject(buttonPath) before click. Not for native store UI; use PurchaseByButton for IAP buy buttons. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.ClickButton( "PopupManager/ShopConfirmPopup(Clone)/Panel/Background/Button Confirm"); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, hub command failed, or click could not run. TimeoutException Object not found before timeoutSeconds elapses. ConnectTestDeviceAsync() Leases a device, starts or reuses an Appium session, and waits for the in-app command hub—without running tests. Declaration public static Task ConnectTestDeviceAsync() Returns Type Description Task Remarks Use from the Test SDK settings window while authoring tests so the first SDK call in a test does not pay full setup cost. After a script change, Unity reloads the domain and clears local SDK state; the controller may still hold the lease and device app. Call this again (or rely on implicit setup on the next SDK call) to re-open the gRPC client and re-sync; existing lease/Appium/hub are reused when possible. ContainsLog(string, int, bool, bool) Returns whether recent Android logcat output from the leased device contains the given text. Declaration public static Task<bool> ContainsLog(string log, int maxLine = 1000, bool clearAfter = false, bool caseSensitive = false) Parameters Type Name Description string log Substring to search for in the captured log text. int maxLine Maximum number of log lines to request from the device (last N in the buffer after filtering). bool clearAfter When true, the Test Controller clears the device log buffer after a successful capture. bool caseSensitive When false, the search uses invariant-culture lowercasing on log only. Returns Type Description Task<bool> True if the captured log contains log; otherwise false. Remarks Uses GetDeviceLogs(int, bool) (Unity tag at Info and above, other tags silenced). On a match, the first matching line is printed to the Unity Console in green. Does not fail the test; combine with NUnit Assert as needed. Examples bool seen = await LHH_TestSDK.ContainsLog("Shop opened", maxLine: 500); Assert.IsTrue(seen); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Log capture failed on the Test Controller. DeleteAllGameData() Deletes every PlayerPrefs entry on the game player. Declaration public static Task DeleteAllGameData() Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Clears all keys, then the player saves. The player build must define DEVELOPMENT_MODE; otherwise the call fails with a message containing "requires DEVELOPMENT_MODE". Examples await LHH_TestSDK.DeleteAllGameData(); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, or the player rejected the delete. DeleteGameData(string) Deletes one PlayerPrefs key on the game player. Declaration public static Task DeleteGameData(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key PlayerPrefs key to remove. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. The player saves after the delete. The player build must define DEVELOPMENT_MODE; otherwise the call fails with a message containing "requires DEVELOPMENT_MODE". Examples await LHH_TestSDK.DeleteGameData("playerName"); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, or the player rejected the delete. GetDeviceLogs(int, bool) Dumps recent Android logcat from the device bound to the current test lease via the Test Controller (ADB). Declaration public static Task<string> GetDeviceLogs(int maxLine = 1000, bool clearAfter = false) Parameters Type Name Description int maxLine Maximum number of log lines to return (last N in the buffer after filtering). bool clearAfter When true, the device log buffer is cleared after a successful dump so the next call sees mostly new logs. Returns Type Description Task<string> Raw logcat text: one line per entry, separated by newline characters. Remarks Filter is fixed to Unity:I *:S (Unity Info/Warn/Error/Fatal; other tags hidden). Android only. For editor-only messages that do not touch the device, use LHH_TestSDK.LogWithColor(System.String,UnityEngine.Color) or LogError(string). Examples string log = await LHH_TestSDK.GetDeviceLogs(maxLine: 1000, clearAfter: true); StringAssert.Contains("IAP initialized", log); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException No leased device, channel error, or log capture failed. GetGameData(string) Reads PlayerPrefs from the game player for the given key (returned as string). Declaration public static Task<string> GetGameData(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key PlayerPrefs key, e.g. coin or heart. Returns Type Description Task<string> Int, float, or string value encoded as string (player tries int, then float, then string). Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Parse in tests with int.TryParse etc. Examples string raw = await LHH_TestSDK.GetGameData("coin"); Assert.IsTrue(int.TryParse(raw, out int coins)); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed or the player could not read the key. GetText(string, float) Waits for a UI object, then reads displayed text from the running game player. Declaration public static Task<string> GetText(string textPath, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string textPath Hierarchy path with / separators (same rules as ClickButton and WaitForObject). float timeoutSeconds Maximum seconds to wait for the object before failing. Returns Type Description Task<string> Text content reported by the player for the object at textPath. Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use, then WaitForObject(textPath) before reading. Supports Unity UI Text and TextMeshPro on the target GameObject. Examples string label = await LHH_TestSDK.GetText("HUD/CoinLabel"); Assert.IsTrue(int.TryParse(label, out int coins)); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, hub command failed, or text could not be read. TimeoutException Object not found before timeoutSeconds elapses. LogError(string) Writes a message to the Unity Console in red (calls LogWithColor with red). Declaration public static void LogError(string message) Parameters Type Name Description string message Text to log. Remarks Use for assertion detail without failing the test until you call NUnit Assert. LogWithColor(string, Color) Writes a message to the Unity Console with the given color (rich text). Declaration public static void LogWithColor(string message, Color color) Parameters Type Name Description string message Text to log. Color color Color applied to the message in the Console window. Remarks Does not contact the Test Controller; safe to use anywhere in a test. Purchase(string) Starts in-app purchase by store catalog product id (no in-game button click). Declaration public static Task Purchase(string catalogProductId) Parameters Type Name Description string catalogProductId IAP product id configured in the game. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Controller sends purchase to the Unity player, then drives the native store sheet. Prefer PurchaseByButton when the test must tap a shop UI element. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.Purchase("com.example.coins_1000"); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentException catalogProductId is null or whitespace. InvalidOperationException Setup failed, purchase failed, or timed out (3 minutes). PurchaseByButton(string) Clicks an in-game shop buy button and completes purchase via the native store UI. Declaration public static Task<bool> PurchaseByButton(string buttonPath) Parameters Type Name Description string buttonPath Hierarchy path to a Unity UI Button (same format as WaitForObject). Returns Type Description Task<bool> True if the Test Controller reports success; false otherwise. Remarks Controller taps the button, waits for the IAP sheet, and confirms buy. Use ClickButton for non-IAP UI. Use Purchase when you have a catalog product id instead of a button path. Examples bool ok = await LHH_TestSDK.PurchaseByButton( "__VIEWS__/Shop/.../Button Buy"); Assert.IsTrue(ok); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, or the purchase client is not initialized. SetGameData(string, int) Writes an int PlayerPrefs value on the game player. Declaration public static Task SetGameData(string key, int value) Parameters Type Name Description string key PlayerPrefs key, e.g. coin or heart. int value Int value stored with PlayerPrefs.SetInt. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. The player saves after the write. The player build must define DEVELOPMENT_MODE; otherwise the call fails with a message containing "requires DEVELOPMENT_MODE". Examples await LHH_TestSDK.SetGameData("coin", 1000); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, or the player rejected the write. SetGameData(string, float) Writes a float PlayerPrefs value on the game player. Declaration public static Task SetGameData(string key, float value) Parameters Type Name Description string key PlayerPrefs key. float value Float value stored with PlayerPrefs.SetFloat. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. The player saves after the write. The player build must define DEVELOPMENT_MODE; otherwise the call fails with a message containing "requires DEVELOPMENT_MODE". Examples await LHH_TestSDK.SetGameData("multiplier", 1.5f); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, or the player rejected the write. SetGameData(string, string) Writes a string PlayerPrefs value on the game player. Declaration public static Task SetGameData(string key, string value) Parameters Type Name Description string key PlayerPrefs key. string value String value stored with PlayerPrefs.SetString. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. The player saves after the write. The player build must define DEVELOPMENT_MODE; otherwise the call fails with a message containing "requires DEVELOPMENT_MODE". Examples await LHH_TestSDK.SetGameData("playerName", "qa"); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, or the player rejected the write. Swipe(int, int, int, int, int) Swipes from one pixel to another on the device screen through Appium. Declaration public static Task Swipe(int fromX, int fromY, int toX, int toY, int durationMs = 300) Parameters Type Name Description int fromX Start horizontal pixel. int fromY Start vertical pixel. int toX End horizontal pixel. int toY End vertical pixel. int durationMs Move duration in milliseconds. Default is 300. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Coordinates are Appium window pixels, origin at the top-left. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.Swipe(540, 1600, 540, 400); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed or the swipe was rejected. TakeScreenshot(string, string) Captures the device screen and writes a PNG on the machine running the Editor. Declaration public static Task<string> TakeScreenshot(string name, string outputDir = null) Parameters Type Name Description string name File name without extension. Saved as {name}.png. string outputDir Directory for the PNG. When null, uses Application.persistentDataPath/Screenshots. Returns Type Description Task<string> Full path of the written PNG file. Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Asks the Test Controller native UI service for a base64 screenshot of the leased device, then decodes and writes the PNG. Creates outputDir when it does not exist. Examples string path = await LHH_TestSDK.TakeScreenshot("home"); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentException name is null or whitespace. InvalidOperationException Setup failed, capture failed, or image data was empty or not valid base64. TapAt(int, int) Taps a pixel on the device screen through Appium. Declaration public static Task TapAt(int x, int y) Parameters Type Name Description int x Horizontal pixel in the Appium window, origin at the top-left. int y Vertical pixel in the Appium window, origin at the top-left. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Coordinates are the Appium window in pixels, not Unity UI positions. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.TapAt(540, 960); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed or the tap was rejected. TapAtNormalized(float, float) Taps a point given as fractions of the device window. Declaration public static Task TapAtNormalized(float x, float y) Parameters Type Name Description float x Horizontal fraction of the Appium window width (0 left, 1 right). float y Vertical fraction of the Appium window height (0 top, 1 bottom). Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Reads the device window size from Appium, then taps that point. 0 is the top-left edge and 1 is the last pixel on that axis. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.TapAtNormalized(0.5f, 0.5f); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, window size could not be read, or the tap was rejected. TapObject(string, float) Waits for an object, reads its Unity screen position, and taps that point through Appium. Declaration public static Task TapObject(string objectPath, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string objectPath Hierarchy path with / separators (same rules as WaitForObject). float timeoutSeconds Maximum seconds to wait for the object before failing. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Polls every 2 seconds. The player returns Camera.main.WorldToScreenPoint of the renderer bounds center, then collider bounds, then transform.position. A RectTransform uses the screen point of its rect center. The result also includes Screen.width and Screen.height. Unity screen coordinates (origin bottom-left) are flipped on Y and scaled to the Appium window, then tapped. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.TapObject("HUD/PlayButton"); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, the screen position could not be read, or the tap was rejected. TimeoutException Object not found before timeoutSeconds elapses. TapObjectDirect(string) Taps an object inside the game player by raising a pointer click or mouse-up message. Declaration public static Task TapObjectDirect(string objectPath) Parameters Type Name Description string objectPath Hierarchy path with / separators (same rules as WaitForObject). Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. The player runs ExecuteEvents.pointerClickHandler when an IPointerClickHandler is found, otherwise SendMessage("OnMouseUpAsButton"). The player build must define DEVELOPMENT_MODE; otherwise the call fails with a message containing "requires DEVELOPMENT_MODE". Examples await LHH_TestSDK.TapObjectDirect("World/Coin"); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, the object was not found, or the player rejected the tap. WaitForObject(string, float) Blocks until a GameObject exists in the game player hierarchy at the given path. Declaration public static Task WaitForObject(string objectPath, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string objectPath Hierarchy path with / separators (same rules as ClickButton). float timeoutSeconds Maximum seconds to wait before throwing. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Polls every 2 seconds. Runs implicit setup on first use. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForObject("iap_manager", timeoutSeconds: 30f); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Implicit setup failed. TimeoutException Object not found before timeoutSeconds elapses. WaitForScene(string, float) Blocks until a loaded scene with the given name is active in the game player. Declaration public static Task WaitForScene(string waitScene, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string waitScene Scene name to match (case-sensitive), compared against all currently loaded scenes. float timeoutSeconds Maximum time to wait before failing the test. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Polls every 2 seconds. Runs implicit setup on first use. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForScene("Home", timeoutSeconds: 50f); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Implicit setup failed, or the game player returned a non-transient error for get-active-scenes ('No Unity app connected' and 'did not respond in time' are retried). TimeoutException No matching scene before timeoutSeconds elapses.

index.html.title: LHH Test SDK | LHH Test SDK
index.html.summary: LHH Test SDK Use LHH_TestSDK from NUnit tests in the Unity Editor to drive a real Android device build through the Test Controller: game UI, waits, PlayerPrefs checks, and in-app purchases. iOS is not supported yet. Section Purpose Manual Install SDK, controller, write and run tests (for QA) Scripting API Generated reference for LHH_TestSDK from XML doc comments in code Before you write tests Add com.lhh.testsdk from Bitbucket and run Install Test SDK (Show Advance Settings). Install Test Controller (Advance Settings), then Run Test Server under Session & server. Set App path (required), bundle id, and optional Test device; use an APK with InAppTestRunner. Optionally Connect test device before running tests. Start with the Manual. Quick example [Test] public async Task Shop_opens_on_home() { await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForScene("Home", timeoutSeconds: 50f); await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForObject("iap_manager"); await LHH_TestSDK.ClickButton("__VIEWS__/Shop/.../Open Shop"); } Requires Unity 2022.3.67f2 or newer.

manual/install-sdk.html.title: Install the Test SDK | LHH Test SDK
manual/install-sdk.html.summary: Install the Test SDK This guide is for QA writing NUnit tests in the Unity Editor with LHH_TestSDK. Platform support: Android only today. iOS options in Settings are reserved for a later release—do not rely on iOS until documented otherwise. Requirements Unity 2022.3 or newer (2022.3.67f2+ recommended). A game project where the player build includes automation (see Player build below). Bitbucket SSH access to LiHuHu repos (for UPM git URLs). 1. Add the Test SDK package In the game project, edit Packages/manifest.json and add: "com.lhh.testsdk": "git@bitbucket.org:lihuhu/lhh-auto-test-sdk.git?path=Assets/TestSDK" Pin a release when dev specifies one, for example: "com.lhh.testsdk": "git@bitbucket.org:lihuhu/lhh-auto-test-sdk.git?path=Assets/TestSDK#v0.1.0" Open the project in Unity and wait for Package Manager to resolve the package. 2. Run Install Test SDK in the Editor Open LHH Test SDK → Settings. Enable Show Advance Settings. Click Install Test SDK and wait until progress shows Test SDK install finished. This step: Writes NuGet config under Assets/ and restores client packages (MagicOnion, MemoryPack, gRPC, etc.). Merges required Unity Package Manager dependencies into Packages/manifest.json. Adds the LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST scripting define so LHH_TestSDK and player hub code compile. You only need to run Install Test SDK again after a SDK update (see Updating after a release). 3. com.lhh.testcontroller.shared (required) The shared contracts package (com.lhh.testcontroller.shared) is not something QA normally adds by hand. Install Test SDK merges it into manifest.json, for example: "com.lhh.testcontroller.shared": "git@bitbucket.org:lihuhu/lhh-auto-test-controller.git?path=src/Lhh.TestController.Shared" It contains MagicOnion service contracts and command DTOs used by: Your NUnit tests (LHH_TestSDK in the Editor), The InAppTestRunner code in the player build, The Test Controller process on your machine. Editor, player, shared package, and running controller must all match the version dev released together. If they drift, you may see hub connection failures or RPC errors. Updating after a release LHH Test SDK → Settings → Check for update compares com.lhh.testsdk, com.lhh.testcontroller.shared, and the Test Controller repo (~/lhh-auto-test-controller) with their git remotes. When something is behind, Update fast-forwards the repo checkouts and refreshes git packages. Stop the test server first. To update those git URLs by hand: Update com.lhh.testsdk in manifest.json (new tag or commit on lhh-auto-test-sdk). Open LHH Test SDK → Settings → Install Test SDK again so installer-owned dependencies stay in sync. Update com.lhh.testcontroller.shared in manifest.json if release notes pin a new controller tag/commit (for example #v0.2.0). Ask the game team for a new Android APK built with the updated automation bits; update App path in Settings before running tests. Confirm in Window → Package Manager that both com.lhh.testsdk and com.lhh.testcontroller.shared are present. Player build (InAppTestRunner) Tests drive a real Android build on a device. That APK must come from a project that: Includes the Test SDK package (which contains InAppTestRunner—hub + command executors for UI, scenes, PlayerPrefs, IAP, etc.). Has LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST enabled for the Android build target (same define Install Test SDK adds for the Editor; the game team must include it on the player platform). At runtime the player should connect to the Test Controller hub (look for logs such as TestSDK: Create MagicOnionCommandHub Done in logcat when debugging). Bundle ID on the device build must match what you configure in Settings (Player Settings application identifier, or Bundle ID override). Next steps Test Controller and settings—install and start the controller, set gRPC, app path, and platform. Writing test cases Running tests

manual/running-tests.html.title: Running tests | LHH Test SDK
manual/running-tests.html.summary: Running tests Android only until a future release documents iOS. Checklist before Run Test SDK installed in the project (Install the Test SDK). com.lhh.testcontroller.shared present and aligned with the SDK/controller version dev released. Install Test Controller done (Advance Settings) and Run Test Server active (Session & server on the Settings window). Android device connected (USB debugging); pick (Any claimable device) or a specific entry under Test device → Refresh device list. Settings filled in: Platform: Android App path: required — automation-enabled APK path valid on the controller machine (InAppTestRunner + LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST on Android) Bundle ID matches the APK (override or Player Settings) gRPC server address: http://127.0.0.1:5050 unless your machine uses another host/port Player build is the version QA expects (rebuild and refresh App path after SDK/shared updates). Optional: Connect test device in Session & server to complete setup before opening the Test Runner. Connect test device (optional, while authoring) Connect test device runs the same pipeline as implicit test setup (lease → Appium → hub) without the Test Runner. Useful when writing tests so the first LHH_TestSDK call in a run is quick. After script recompile, use Re-sync test device. The controller may still hold your lease; the Editor reconnects and reuses an active Appium session when possible. Release session now when you want the device back without stopping the whole test server. Run from Test Runner Window → General → Test Runner Select EditMode (or PlayMode if your team uses it for specific tests). Run one test, a fixture, or all tests. If setup already succeeded in this Unity domain (Connect test device or an earlier test), subsequent SDK calls skip setup until Release session now, domain reload, or CleanUpAfterTest. Otherwise the first SDK call in the run performs setup. Failures during lease or Appium create fail the test immediately (NUnit error)—fix Settings or controller state before retrying. When the entire run completes (pass or fail), the device is returned automatically only if Release session after test run is checked in Settings. If that option is off, the lease stays until you use Release session now or turn the option back on for the next run. What “good” looks like Unity Console: Test SDK: Test device session is ready. (or prior connect), then test logs/assertions. Device: APK launches on first session create; UI responds to Editor-driven commands. Settings shows Editor session — Ready for SDK calls in this domain after Connect test device succeeds. Troubleshooting Symptom Things to check Test SDK App path is empty… Set App path before running tests or Connect test device. Path must exist on the machine running the Test Controller. Test device assignment failed / lease message from controller No claimable device; wrong Selected device; another session holding the pool; controller not running. Refresh device list. Appium session was not created / message from controller Bad APK path, install failure, Appium/device error—read the exception text and controller logs. Appium session already active; skipping create Stale session on device. Release session now, Stop Test Server, or reinstall launch; then Connect test device again. Command hub is not connected APK without InAppTestRunner / automation define; wrong bundle id; app crashed; firewall blocking gRPC. Timed out waiting for object/scene Wrong path (Extract Object Path); increase timeout; game not on expected scene. Failed to click button Path not a Button; object inactive. Purchase failures PurchaseByButton / Purchase; sandbox account; up to 3 minutes for Purchase. RPC / type errors after upgrade Update com.lhh.testsdk and com.lhh.testcontroller.shared, re-run Install Test SDK, restart server, new APK. For controller-side logs, use Progress (Advance Settings) or ~/lhh-auto-test-controller/.run/ when using the installed controller repo. Reference Scripting API — LHH_TestSDK — full method list and parameters.

manual/test-controller-and-settings.html.title: Test Controller and settings | LHH Test SDK
manual/test-controller-and-settings.html.summary: Test Controller and settings Android only for running tests today. Open Settings LHH Test SDK → Settings Values are stored in EditorPrefs on your machine (not in git). Each QA machine keeps its own gRPC address, app path, bundle id, and device preference. Configuration (always visible) Field Purpose gRPC server address Test Controller URL. Default: http://127.0.0.1:5050. Bundle ID Optional override. If empty, the effective id is Player Settings → Application identifier. Must match the installed APK. Platform Use Android for now. App path Required for setup. Full path to the automation-enabled .apk as the Test Controller host can read it (use Browse). If empty, the first setup call fails the test with an error—there is no silent continue. Release session after test run When enabled (default), the Test Runner returns the leased device when a full run finishes or the runner errors. Turn off to keep the lease between runs (see Release session now to return the device manually). Test device (device pool) Shown under Configuration when the test server is ready. Control Purpose Selected device (Any claimable device) or a specific device from the controller pool. This is a preference only—the lease happens on Connect test device or on the first LHH_TestSDK call in a test. Refresh device list Reloads claimable devices from the controller (devices already leased are omitted). Requires Test Controller installed and Run Test Server active. If the server is not running, the list is disabled and a warning explains why. Changing Platform while the server is running refreshes the device list automatically. Session & server Visible on the main Settings page (not hidden under Advance Settings). Control Purpose Connect test device / Re-sync test device Runs setup without the Test Runner: lease device (using Selected device if set), Appium session, hub wait. Label switches to Re-sync when the Editor domain already completed setup. Use while authoring tests so the first API call in a test is faster. Release session now Returns the leased device to the pool and clears Editor setup state immediately. Run Test Server / Stop Test Server Starts or stops Appium and the controller (gRPC 5050, Appium 4723). Shown after Install Test Controller succeeds. Domain reload: After you change scripts, Unity clears local SDK state. The controller may still hold the lease and an Appium session. Use Re-sync test device before the next test, or let implicit setup run on the first SDK call. If Appium reports a session already active but the wrong app is on the device, Stop Test Server or Release session now, then connect again. Updates Check for update compares three git sources with their remotes: Source What is compared com.lhh.testsdk Installed package revision, or this repo when the project is the Test SDK checkout com.lhh.testcontroller.shared Installed package revision in packages-lock.json Test Controller repo ~/lhh-auto-test-controller against origin of the current branch If any source is behind, Update appears. Otherwise the window reports that you are up to date. Stop the test server before updating the shared package or the Test Controller repo. After a Test SDK package update, run Install Test SDK again if installer-owned dependencies changed, and install a new player build before testing. Install Test Controller and Test SDK (Advance Settings) Enable Show Advance Settings at the bottom of the window: Control Purpose Install Test SDK NuGet/UPM merge and LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST (see Install the Test SDK). Install Test Controller Clones and prepares ~/lhh-auto-test-controller (environment check/setup). Progress Log output for install/setup. Typical order: Install Test SDK → Install Test Controller → Run Test Server (in Session & server) → set App path and device → Connect test device (optional) → run tests. If controller install fails, read Progress. Missing JDK, Android SDK, or Appium usually needs a one-time machine setup—coordinate with dev/infra. The running controller version should match com.lhh.testcontroller.shared in your Unity project (see Install the Test SDK). What happens during setup Whether you use Connect test device or the first LHH_TestSDK call in a test, setup: Opens a gRPC client to gRPC server address. Requests a device lease from the controller (with optional Selected device id). If leasing fails, the test stops immediately with the controller’s message (for example no free device). Appium session — if none is active for your bundle id, creates one using App path (must be set) and launches the APK. If a session is already active, creation is skipped (see warning in Console if the device state is wrong). Waits until the Unity player command hub connects. When the Test Runner finishes the whole run (or reports a runner error), the SDK calls Release session logic only if Release session after test run is enabled. Next steps Writing test cases Running tests

manual/writing-tests.html.title: Writing test cases | LHH Test SDK
manual/writing-tests.html.summary: Writing test cases Tests are ordinary NUnit tests in the Unity Editor. They call static methods on LHH_TestSDK to control the game on a connected Android device. API details: Scripting API — LHH_TestSDK. Where to put tests Add a test assembly under your project, for example Assets/Tests/..., with references to Unity Test Framework and the Test SDK assemblies (follow how your game repo already sets up Edit Mode tests). Edit Mode vs Play Mode Most automation tests run in Edit Mode so the Editor drives the device while the game runs on hardware: [Test] [RequiresPlayMode(false)] public async Task Example_flow() { await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForScene("Home", timeoutSeconds: 50f); await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForObject("iap_manager"); await LHH_TestSDK.ClickButton("__VIEWS__/Shop/.../Button Open"); } Use async Task test methods and await every SDK call. Typical flow Wait for state — WaitForScene, WaitForObject (poll every 2 seconds until timeout). Act — ClickButton for normal UI; IAP shop buy flows use PurchaseByButton or Purchase. Assert — NUnit Assert.* on values from GetGameData, GetText, or your own helpers. Seed or clear PlayerPrefs with SetGameData, DeleteGameData, and DeleteAllGameData when the test needs a known value. Example reading and writing PlayerPrefs on the device: await LHH_TestSDK.SetGameData("coin", 1000); await LHH_TestSDK.SetGameData("multiplier", 1.5f); await LHH_TestSDK.SetGameData("playerName", "qa"); string raw = await LHH_TestSDK.GetGameData("coin"); Assert.IsTrue(int.TryParse(raw, out int coins)); Assert.GreaterOrEqual(coins, 1000); await LHH_TestSDK.DeleteGameData("playerName"); await LHH_TestSDK.DeleteAllGameData(); SetGameData, DeleteGameData, and DeleteAllGameData write PlayerPrefs in the player and the player calls PlayerPrefs.Save. The player build must define DEVELOPMENT_MODE as well as LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST. If DEVELOPMENT_MODE is missing, the call fails with a message that contains requires DEVELOPMENT_MODE. DeleteAllGameData removes every PlayerPrefs key on the device. Hierarchy paths (buttons and objects) Paths use / between hierarchy segments, same rules for WaitForObject, ClickButton, and GetText: Root objects: path segment matches GameObject.Find. Children: resolved with Transform.Find under the previous segment. Copy paths from the Editor: LHH Test SDK → Extract Object Path Or GameObject → LHH Test SDK → Extract Object Path with a object selected. Paste the copied string into your test constants. Real projects often use long paths under prefixes such as __VIEWS__/.... UI clicks vs in-app purchase Goal API Tap a normal Unity UI button ClickButton(path) Tap shop buy + complete native store sheet PurchaseByButton(path) Purchase by store product id (no button path) Purchase(catalogProductId) Do not use ClickButton for IAP buy buttons that must trigger the native store UI—use PurchaseByButton. Logging during investigation These only write to the Unity Console; they do not talk to the controller: LHH_TestSDK.LogWithColor("checkpoint A", Color.cyan); LHH_TestSDK.LogError("coins before assert: " + coins); Screenshots TakeScreenshot captures the device screen through the Test Controller and writes a PNG on the Editor machine: string path = await LHH_TestSDK.TakeScreenshot("home"); The file is {name}.png. When outputDir is omitted, the folder is Application.persistentDataPath/Screenshots. The directory is created if needed, and the call returns the full path. Device gestures TapAt, TapAtNormalized, and Swipe drive the leased device through Appium. Coordinates are the Appium window in pixels, origin at the top-left, not Unity hierarchy positions. await LHH_TestSDK.TapAt(540, 960); await LHH_TestSDK.TapAtNormalized(0.5f, 0.5f); await LHH_TestSDK.Swipe(540, 1600, 540, 400); await LHH_TestSDK.Swipe(540, 1600, 540, 400, durationMs: 500); TapAtNormalized reads the device window size from Appium, then taps that fraction of the window (0 is the top-left edge, 1 is the last pixel on that axis). Swipe moves from one pixel to another; durationMs defaults to 300. Timeouts WaitForScene, WaitForObject, ClickButton, and GetText accept optional timeoutSeconds (default 30). Increase for slow loads or heavy scenes. Next step Running tests
